title: The brick mall
content: The toy store was two stories with a circular view to the bottom, and stuffed animals line the shelves that were dark and tall. Like a Barnes and noble, well lit. A food court with a long, white and shiny were the floors. There was a floor like that, and another floor built like an old train station. There was a shop of tricks and games and the best stuff was up the stairs at the back. The two doors on that little ledge. I don’t know what was in there but it felt like people. There’s an amusement park in the sky, lonely and cold. There’s a big pool room all pink and mint and open and huge with deep pools, set against a windowed wall. You can see the pool like you would at an aquarium. Abandoned homes beautiful on the outside and torn on the inside. Sometimes when I’m here I know there’s nobody else but I can feel them ready to chase me out of their home. I run through dirt trails and mud and a shallow lake to get to and fro. I remember one thing and my journey through the mud and then I experience the next thing.
